digest.component_or_area: MCP error handling and CLI/library/MCP cross-interface consistency
propositions: MCP tool failures currently lack a machine-readable error code discriminator, forcing agents to pattern-match English text; the CLI already emits `error_envelope` with a `error` code field, and MCP must emit the same discriminator from an identical vocabulary

Error codes are scattered across CLI call sites (ticket_not_found, show_failed, deps_failed, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, and CommandError.error_code values) with no central registry or library-side exposure, violating the AC that a code cannot exist on one interface only and preventing three-way cross-interface tests

TicketNotFoundError must be a distinct ReadError subclass raised only at the two genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) so error_code_for can classify by isinstance rather than message substring, making the machine code independent of human message wording

MCP's two ad-hoc soft-error shapes (_mcp_reads.py explain_criterion returning {error, kind}, _mcp_llm.py returning {error, ...}) must be migrated to carry a KNOWN_ERROR_CODES member in the error field while preserving their existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

The guard wrapping each MCP tool body must catch rebar exceptions and raise McpEnvelopeError whose .envelope dict is built via error_envelope(error_code_for(exc), input_or_empty, str(exc), returncode) and whose __str__ returns JSON, delivering the envelope on ToolError.__cause__ for consumption via pytest.raises(ToolError).__cause__.envelope

CLI envelope output must remain byte-identical (reads_cli.py:410 message-keyed distinction between ticket_not_found and deps_failed is preserved, TicketNotFoundError raised with the same message string as the prior ReadError), verified by a regression test
